record_type_quote: In a replication of Feldman-Summers and Pope's (1994) national survey of American Psychologists on ‘forgetting’ childhood abuse, a Dutch sample of 500 members of the Netherlands Institute of Psychologists (NIP), were asked if they had been abused as children, and, if so, whether they had ever forgotten some or all of the abuse for some significant period of time.

targets.title: The experience of ‘forgetting’ child abuse: A national survey of psychologists
targets.evidence_quote: In a replication of Feldman-Summers and Pope's (1994) national survey of American Psychologists on ‘forgetting’ childhood abuse, a Dutch sample of 500 members of the Netherlands Institute of Psychologists (NIP), were asked if they had been abused as children, and, if so, whether they had ever forgotten some or all of the abuse for some significant period of time.
targets.outcome_quote: These results were remarkably similar to the results of | Feldman-Summers and Pope's original study.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The abstract gives an overall similarity verdict, reinforced by the conclusion that the current study converges with the US survey. This takes precedence over differences in individual comparisons.

reasoning: Verified title and all four authors in scanned article. Dutch psychologist sample re-tests the explicitly designated American survey. OCR includes layout artifacts; all ten pages including references retained.
